To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GH replacement therapy in adults with GH deficiency results in a significant decrease in bone mineral density, which is not prevented by treatment with the bisphosphonic acid pamidronate.
the combined treatment of GH and bisphosphonates in GH‐deficent adults has beneficial effects on bone mass, bone turnover, and renal phosphate handling, compared to GH treatment alone.
the addition of Pamidronate to the treatment of GHD subjects receiving GH replacement therapy does not improve renal phosphate handling, but does decrease bone turnover and increase BMD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of GH on the development of the skeleton, the role of IGF-I and IGF binding proteins in this process and the effects of GH and IGF-I on osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and osteocytes.
the development of new methods for the detection of the most important biomarkers of human diseases and their application to medical diagnostics, drug discovery and personalized medicine.
the development of novel, selective inhibitors of GH action for treatment of acromegaly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GH replacement therapy in GHD patients is associated with an increased bone turnover, which is accompanied by a decrease in bone mass and an increased risk of fracture.
GH deficiency is associated with an increase in bone turnover and a decrease in bone mass in adults and children.
there is a lack of evidence that GH replacement therapy is beneficial in adults with GHD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of pamindronate to GH therapy in adults with GHD does not have a negative effect on renal phosphate handling.
the combination of growth hormone and bisphosphonates is an effective treatment for bone loss in adults with growth hormone deficiency.
the addition of pamindronate to the GH treatment did not improve the bone mass or turnover in GHD adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of GH and bisphosphonates may provide a novel therapeutic option for patients with GH deficiency and osteoporosis, with the advantage of a more favorable side effect profile than that of GH alone.
GH deficiency in adults is associated with a significant decrease in bone density and that the combination of GH and pamidronate is effective at preventing bone loss in these subjects.
